plugin.blake2.title: BLAKE2s and BLAKE2b
plugin.blake2.preset.blake2s-256-empty: BLAKE2s-256 of the empty message (one all-zero block)
plugin.blake2.preset.blake2s-256-keyed: BLAKE2s-256 with a 32-byte key (reference test vector)
plugin.blake2.preset.blake2b-512-abc-rou: BLAKE2b-512 of “abc”, one step per round
plugin.blake2.param.algorithmHint: BLAKE2s works on 32-bit words (10 rounds, 64-byte blocks), BLAKE2b on 64-bit words (12 rounds, 128-byte blocks). The digest length is part of the parameter block, so BLAKE2b-256 is not a truncated BLAKE2b-512.
plugin.blake2.param.encodingHint: Text is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Hex lets you enter any bytes, two hex digits per byte.
plugin.blake2.param.inputHint: 0 to 128 bytes. The message may be empty.
plugin.blake2.param.keyHint: Empty for plain hashing. Up to 32 bytes for BLAKE2s and 64 bytes for BLAKE2b; the key, padded with zeros, becomes the first block.
plugin.blake2.param.detailHint: “Per G call” shows each of the eight G calls of every round. “Per round” runs a whole round in one step. “Per block” runs all rounds of a block in one step.
plugin.blake2.op.init: Set h to the IV and the parameter block
plugin.blake2.op.load: Load the block and fill the working vector v
plugin.blake2.op.g: Mix four words of v with the G function
plugin.blake2.op.compress: Run all rounds of the block
plugin.blake2.step.initial: {{algorithm}} turns the {{bytes}}-byte message into a {{bits}}-bit hash value. It cuts the message into {{blockBytes}}-byte blocks (the last one padded with zeros) and compresses each block in {{rounds}} rounds. Each round mixes a 4 × 4 matrix of {{wordBits}}-bit words with eight calls of the G function, using only addition, XOR and rotation (ARX).
plugin.blake2.step.initialKeyed: {{algorithm}} turns the {{bytes}}-byte message and a {{keyBytes}}-byte key into a {{bits}}-bit hash value. The key, padded with zeros, becomes the first {{blockBytes}}-byte block (RFC 7693 §3.3); the message blocks follow. Each block is compressed in {{rounds}} rounds of eight G calls on a 4 × 4 matrix of {{wordBits}}-bit words.
plugin.blake2.step.init: h starts as the IV (the {{algorithm}} constants, equal to the SHA-2 initial hash values), with h₀ XORed with parameter word 0 = {{p}}: digest length nn = {{nn}} bytes, key length kk = {{kk}} bytes, fanout 1 and depth 1 (RFC 7693 §2.5). h = {{h}}.
plugin.blake2.step.load: Block {{n}}: {{bytes}} of its {{blockBytes}} bytes are message bytes. v₀ … v₇ ← h, v₈ … v₁₅ ← IV. The counter t = {{t}} bytes so far goes into v₁₂ ⊕= t₀ = {{t0}} and v₁₃ ⊕= t₁ = {{t1}}. More blocks follow, so v₁₄ stays IV₆.
plugin.blake2.step.loadLast: Block {{n}} is the last block: {{bytes}} of its {{blockBytes}} bytes are message bytes, the rest are zeros. v₀ … v₇ ← h, v₈ … v₁₅ ← IV, v₁₂ ⊕= t₀ = {{t0}} and v₁₃ ⊕= t₁ = {{t1}} with t = {{t}} bytes in total, and v₁₄ is inverted (⊕ all ones): the final-block flag. The counter and the flag make every block position distinct, so no padding with a length field is needed.
plugin.blake2.step.loadKey: Block {{n}} is the key, padded with zeros to {{blockBytes}} bytes. v₀ … v₇ ← h, v₈ … v₁₅ ← IV. The counter counts the key block as a full block: t = {{t}}, so v₁₂ ⊕= t₀ = {{t0}} and v₁₃ ⊕= t₁ = {{t1}}. Message blocks follow, so v₁₄ stays IV₆.
plugin.blake2.step.loadKeyLast: Block {{n}} is the key, padded with zeros to {{blockBytes}} bytes, and the message is empty, so it is also the last block. v₀ … v₇ ← h, v₈ … v₁₅ ← IV, v₁₂ ⊕= t₀ = {{t0}} and v₁₃ ⊕= t₁ = {{t1}} with t = {{t}}, and v₁₄ is inverted: the final-block flag.
plugin.blake2.step.loadEmpty: The message is empty and there is no key, so BLAKE2 compresses a single all-zero block. v₀ … v₇ ← h, v₈ … v₁₅ ← IV, the counter t = 0 leaves v₁₂ and v₁₃ unchanged, and v₁₄ is inverted: the final-block flag.
plugin.blake2.step.gColumn: Round {{round}} (σ[{{s}}]), G{{i}} on column {{i}}: v{{a}}, v{{b}}, v{{c}}, v{{d}} with x = m{{xi}} = {{x}} and y = m{{yi}} = {{y}}. G adds x, XORs and rotates right by {{r1}} and {{r2}}, then adds y, XORs and rotates right by {{r3}} and {{r4}}. New: v{{a}} = {{a2}}, v{{b}} = {{b2}}, v{{c}} = {{c2}}, v{{d}} = {{d2}}.
plugin.blake2.step.gDiagonal: Round {{round}} (σ[{{s}}]), G{{i}} on a diagonal: v{{a}}, v{{b}}, v{{c}}, v{{d}} with x = m{{xi}} = {{x}} and y = m{{yi}} = {{y}}. After the four column calls, the diagonal calls mix words from different columns. New: v{{a}} = {{a2}}, v{{b}} = {{b2}}, v{{c}} = {{c2}}, v{{d}} = {{d2}} (rotations {{r1}}, {{r2}}, {{r3}}, {{r4}}).
plugin.blake2.step.round: Round {{round}}: the message words in the order σ[{{s}}], four G calls on the columns of v, then four on the diagonals. v = {{v}}.
plugin.blake2.step.compress: Block {{n}}: all {{rounds}} rounds in one step. Afterwards v = {{v}}.
plugin.blake2.step.feedForward: Feed-forward after block {{n}}: hⱼ ← hⱼ ⊕ vⱼ ⊕ vⱼ₊₈ for j = 0 … 7, so h = {{h}}. Folding both halves of v into the old h makes the compression function hard to invert.
plugin.blake2.step.output: The {{algorithm}} hash value is h after block {{n}}, written as little-endian bytes: all {{bytes}} bytes, {{digest}}.
plugin.blake2.step.outputTruncated: The {{algorithm}} hash value is h after block {{n}}, written as little-endian bytes and cut to its first {{bytes}} bytes: {{digest}}.
plugin.blake2.formula.load: v₀…v₇ ← h; v₈…v₁₅ ← IV; v₁₂ ⊕= t₀; v₁₃ ⊕= t₁ (block {{n}})
plugin.blake2.formula.loadLast: v₀…v₇ ← h; v₈…v₁₅ ← IV; v₁₂ ⊕= t₀; v₁₃ ⊕= t₁; v₁₄ ⊕= f₀ (block {{n}}, last)
plugin.blake2.formula.round: Round {{round}}: G₀ … G₃ on the columns, G₄ … G₇ on the diagonals, σ[{{s}}]

plugin.blake2.error.encoding: Unknown input format “{{encoding}}”: choose text or hex.
plugin.blake2.error.inputLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 bytes are allowed.
